Use Tier 2: add a jointly trained, recency-aware history encoder to the existing LightGCN model. Focus on model_design and training_evaluation as one controlled architectural change. The graph model achieves 0.59 macro HR@10, but Electronics falls to 0.39 versus the SASRec baseline’s 0.42, suggesting that discarding sequence information may limit performance. Its current known-user prediction ignores the supplied history, preventing adaptation to recent interests.

Keep graph propagation and add attention pooling over the most recent history items, using the propagated item embeddings and learned relative-position embeddings. Fuse this history representation with the graph user embedding through a learned gate, producing one user vector scored against the same item embeddings and jointly learned item bias. Train the complete network end to end with the existing sampled-softmax objective, sampling training-sequence cut points and supplying only the preceding prefix to the history encoder. This preserves collaborative information while allowing the network to learn when recent behavior should influence recommendations.

Use the same history processing during validation and hosted prediction, and update the predictor writer to reconstruct the augmented architecture. Preserve all four categories, fixed seeds, input splits, DATA_DIR, and validation candidate protocol; select one checkpoint per category using validation HR@10 and report the four-category macro average. Each category must load exactly one jointly trained model, with no separate score sources or checkpoint averaging. Leave held-out prediction to the host without reading test files or generating a fabricated submission.
